source.title: Scaling Behavior of Discrete Diffusion Language Models
source.authors: Dimitri von Rütte; J. Fluri; Omead Brandon Pooladzandi; Bernhard Schölkopf; Thomas Hofmann; Antonio Orvieto

record.tranche_reason: The study measures scaling relations and compute-optimal allocations for discrete diffusion language models, testing the same general scaling questions with a different model objective and a negative-ELBO loss measure.
record.gate_note: The study reports its own fitted loss-scaling exponents, compute-optimal parameter and token exponents, large-run validation, and downstream benchmark results. It also cites scaling results for autoregressive models and other studies; cited results are not cataloged as this study's measurements. The study's loss measure is negative ELBO, an upper bound on NLL, rather than held-out cross-entropy.
record.test_reason: The study fits its own iso-FLOP scaling laws (Hoffmann Approach 2) for discrete diffusion language models, a new model family, on the negative ELBO. It reports compute-optimal allocation exponents, checks the fits against 3B and 10B runs, compares FLOP-counting and smoothing choices, and evaluates downstream benchmarks. It is text pretraining with a different generative objective, so it tests V1, V2, V3, V6 and V7 in a new setting rather than with the original method and measure.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that all diffusion noise types reach similar loss scaling in compute-bound settings. More uniform noise needs more parameters and less data at compute-optimality, and is best in token-bound settings. Diffusion LMs are more parameter-heavy than autoregressive laws. The fits predict 3B/10B runs up to 50× larger. DLMs, especially uniform diffusion, are competitive with and may overtake ALMs.
record.recipe_differences: The study applies scaling-law fitting to discrete diffusion models and negative ELBO, rather than autoregressive next-token models and held-out cross-entropy. It uses iso-FLOP profiles, tuned batch size and learning rate, CompleteP, and compares two FLOP-counting approaches and raw versus smoothed fits.
record.method_sensitivity: Noise type changes the fitted allocation and loss exponents. The study reports sensitivity to FLOP-counting method (M = 6P versus M = 6P + 12LDN), raw versus smoothed iso-FLOP observations, data composition, and whether an irreducible term is fitted. It finds learning-rate annealing shifts loss by a reported constant factor while leaving optimal hyperparameters largely unchanged.

fits_no_version.finding: The optimal batch size scales as a power law of training tokens (B* ∝ D^0.82, R² 0.975), largely independent of model size and loss. The optimal learning rate scales as B*^0.34. Iso-loss batch/step pairs follow a hyperbola.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Compute-optimal hyperparameters (batch size, learning rate) follow predictable power laws in training tokens.

record.problems: The fitted loss is negative ELBO rather than held-out cross-entropy. The main sweep covers five model sizes from 25M to 570M non-embedding parameters; the large-run prediction check is reported in figures without numerical loss values in the text. The authors note that scaling coefficients can vary with dataset composition and that some fits are sensitive to FLOP estimation and smoothing choices.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted other Table 7 combinations of token- and parameter-count exponents for Method 2 and raw fits, plus detailed alternate fits in Appendix D, to stay within the 60-row cap. Also omitted the reported 0% HumanEval pass rate for the three checkpoints; it is a downstream result but not needed alongside the extracted benchmark rows.

untested.parts: Held-out cross-entropy of autoregressive models. The study fits negative ELBO (an NLL upper bound) for diffusion LMs. Separate loss-vs-N and loss-vs-D laws are not fitted; only compute-frontier loss is.
All of it. There is no controlled depth/width comparison at fixed parameter count.
All of it. Only text pretraining; no other modality, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer.
Quantitative prediction of downstream scores from scale or loss. Only three checkpoints, with no fit.
The effect of data composition on exponents (mentioned but not tested). Bending away from a power law is not observed: the irreducible term fits ≈0.

missing.what: Learning-rate annealing (20% cooldown) gives a constant 2.45% ± 0.14% loss improvement and leaves optimal hyperparameters unchanged; the ratio holds at 3B/10B (y/x = 1.0245, R² 0.988). This is a schedule-choice result.
Fitting with an irreducible term gives E ≈ 0 for smoothed fits, but nonzero E (about 0.4–0.6) and steeper α (about -0.06) for raw loss fits.
Goodness of fit: R² about 0.9996 for loss-vs-compute fits; R² 0.89–0.998 for allocation fits.
The likelihood gap between masked and uniform diffusion shrinks from 3.2% at 1e18 FLOPs to 1.7% at 1e21 FLOPs.
Method 2 and raw-data allocation exponents differ from Method 1, e.g. masked P* exponent 0.597 vs 0.623, uniform D* exponent 0.382 vs 0.411.

record.verdict_notes: Main correction: Table 7's 'Tokens (D)' and 'Non-emb. params (P)' blocks are compute-optimal allocation exponents versus compute, not loss-vs-D or loss-vs-P exponents. The D-* and P-* rows therefore move from V1 to V3, and the D-* rows duplicate the DSTAR-* rows. V5 is not tested: the diffusion objective is still text pretraining. The record's V1 limits_scope for NELBO versus cross-entropy is a difference in what was measured, so it is listed as untested rather than as a limit. Table 1 comparisons to Hoffmann, DeepSeek, Nie and Ni are cited values and are not rows. The M3/U3 benchmark rows serve as baselines, not standalone results.

versions.untested_parts: The study fits negative-ELBO rather than held-out cross-entropy, and does not establish the same relationship for autoregressive language models.
Validation is shown for the study's discrete diffusion models and reported as close agreement; it does not validate every noise type or the original autoregressive models.
The study tests compute-optimal allocation for its diffusion models, not the full range of training setups or the original autoregressive parameter/data trends.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study tests discrete diffusion as an alternative text-pretraining objective; it does not test other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
The study reports a set of NLP benchmark results and a qualitative association with ELBO, but does not fit a quantitative downstream-versus-loss or downstream-versus-scale prediction.
The study compares selected fitting and FLOP-counting choices; it does not test every data, schedule, or fitting choice mentioned in the version.

relationships.condition: Five diffusion noise types, 25M–570M non-embedding parameters, about 1e17–1e21 FLOPs; Method 1 and Method 2, raw and smoothed fits
relationships.reason: Compute-frontier NELBO follows L ∝ C^α, with α of about -0.046 to -0.052 across all fits (C-*, CR-*, C2-*); Table 8 R² is about 0.9996 (text).
